scenes.text: Albert Einstein invented a fridge, and its patent was granted on November eleventh, nineteen thirty.
He designed it with his former student, the physicist Leo Szilard.
Fun fact: years earlier, Einstein had worked as a clerk in a Swiss patent office.
It began with a newspaper story about a Berlin family killed by gas leaking from their fridge.
Back then, many fridges used poisonous gases and pumps with seals that could fail.
So Einstein and Szilard designed a fridge with no moving parts at all.
Instead of a motor, it runs on a simple source of heat, like a small gas flame.
Inside, three fluids do all the work: ammonia, butane and water.
The pair filed many patents together, and the Swedish company Electrolux bought one of them.
But in the nineteen thirties, a new gas called Freon made ordinary fridges much safer.
So Einstein's fridge never made it into everyday kitchens.
Decades later, engineers at Oxford University started working on a modern version.
Because it can run on heat alone, it could help where electricity is scarce.
Would you keep your snacks in a fridge designed by Albert Einstein?

title: Einstein invented a fridge with no moving parts 🧊
caption: On Nov 11, 1930, Albert Einstein and Leo Szilard got a US patent for a fridge with no moving parts, powered by heat. It was inspired by a news story about a deadly fridge gas leak. 🧊
